video.title: How to Find the Best Undervalued Deals (For Beginners)

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates how he finds potential off-market RV park acquisitions by scraping Google Maps listings, cleaning and validating phone data, then texting owners and following up by phone. He screens a prospect by asking about occupancy, seasonal pricing, utilities, acreage, and operations, and explains his target of at least a 10% cap rate. A seller describes a seasonal lakeside campground with 80–85% occupancy and different prices for shoreline and inland sites. The video offers a practical sourcing workflow, but the demo does not show a completed acquisition, and several response-rate figures are inconsistent.

ideas.name: Off-market RV park acquisition
ideas.one_liner: Find RV park owners through map listings, contact them directly, and evaluate potential acquisitions against a target cap rate.
ideas.business_model: Buy income-producing RV parks and earn revenue from site rentals. Seller financing is discussed as a possible way to reduce cash required at purchase, not as a guaranteed outcome.
ideas.customer: For deal sourcing, RV park owners who may consider selling. After acquisition, campers and RV owners who rent sites.
ideas.problem: The buyer needs a repeatable way to find and assess parks that are not listed for sale. The sellers' specific problems are not stated.
ideas.offer: Approach park owners directly, learn about the property's occupancy and operations, and consider an offer based on net operating income and other value levers. Koerner says he targets at least a 10% cap rate.

pricing.model: Acquisition price based on property income and a target cap rate; ongoing income from rented sites.

price_points.unit: annual net profit in illustrative example
price_points.label: Example income used to discuss valuation

price_points.unit: purchase price ceiling in illustrative example
price_points.label: Koerner says he would try to pay under this amount for the example

pricing.notes: The $100,000 income and under-$1 million purchase price are an illustrative calculation, not a reported transaction.

acquisition_channels.details: Uses Outscraper's Google Maps data scraper to find RV parks by category and state, then reviews listing fields such as phone type, owner verification, ratings, and photos.

quote.text: So this is outscraper and I want to show you how I use outs scraper but then I didn't want to have to wait for it to scrape.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Filters for cell numbers, adds a city name as a personalized variable, and sends a short first text to start a conversation. He follows up with people who respond. In the UK, unsolicited marketing texts to individuals and sole traders require consent under PECR.

quote.text: The best results come when you're willing to play the long game and just seek to start a conversation on the first message as opposed to ask them right up front if they're interested in selling.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Calls a seller who asks to speak by phone; Koerner says he researches the property before calling. This is a response to the seller, not a cold call.

quote.text: Give me a call. I don't do business over text message. Okay, I will. I like to do a little more research before I call them so I don't sound like an idiot.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The video focuses on finding and assessing acquisition targets. After purchase, the owner would operate the park and rent sites; the transcript does not explain Koerner's post-purchase staffing, maintenance, or guest-service process. The seller in the example says he manages his park seasonally.
unit_economics_claims: Koerner says he targets a minimum 10% cap rate.
He illustrates that $100,000 in annual net profit would imply trying to pay under $1 million.
A capped Outscraper search in the demo is quoted at $10; this is lead-list cost, not a full business startup cost.
He says 129 scraped listings yielded 129 cell phones from a 500-listing search, or 26%.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated. The demonstrated scrape is quoted at $10 for a search capped at 500 listings; this is not a complete startup-cost estimate.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated for a purchase or operating revenue. The demonstrated scrape is quoted as taking 7–25 minutes.

acquisition.how: Map scraping and data cleaning can be automated, but the demonstrated unsolicited SMS approach is restricted in the UK for individuals and sole traders without consent. UK cold email to limited companies may be used where appropriate; cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS. Seller negotiation remains human.

onboarding.how: Property records, financials, site visits, and purchase documents require human review and negotiation; no automated onboarding process is described.

delivery.how: Operating an RV park involves physical property, utilities, and guest needs. The video does not describe automation for that work.

billing.how: No billing system is described. Site rental billing could use software, but setup and exceptions would need human oversight.

support.how: Guest and seller conversations are handled personally in the example; no automated support system is described.

uk_applicability.notes: The property-investment and map-research approach can work in the UK, but the demonstrated US cold-text workflow cannot be copied to UK individuals and sole traders without consent under PECR. UK cold email can be used for limited companies, and cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS. Property, planning, and seasonal-demand assumptions also need local assessment.

risks: The transcript presents seller financing as a possibility, not a guaranteed way to buy with no money down.
The example's reply figures do not reconcile: four initial replies from 129 recipients are described as a 10% response rate, and a later count is 23 responses.
The speaker says listing owner names may be missing or inaccurate, data can include the wrong business category, and duplicate phone rows can disrupt data matching.
The demonstrated cold SMS tactic would require a UK-compliant lawful basis and appropriate consent where the recipient is an individual or sole trader.
The demonstration does not establish the seller's asking price, net operating income, required capital works, or whether a deal closes.

tactics.name: Build a bounded Google Maps lead list
steps: Choose a Google Maps business category such as RV park and select a target state.
Set a result cap before scraping to limit accidental spend.
Select useful fields such as phone, address, category, rating, review count, photos, owner verification, and phone carrier type.
Review categories after export because the scraper can include adjacent business types.

quote.text: And then it's probably a good idea to cap your results just so you don't accidentally spend a bunch of money. I capped it at 500.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Clean and validate phone data before outreach
steps: Standardize phone formatting in the spreadsheet.
Remove duplicate phone numbers before matching validation results back to the list.
Upload only rows with phone numbers to Sly Broadcast for carrier-type validation.
Check that the validated numbers remain aligned with the correct listings.

quote.text: And so, I'm just going to kind of do a cursory glance. Oh, and they're not. Oh, okay. Yep. There's duplicates. That's why.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Personalize the first text and keep it short
steps: Use a reliable field such as city for personalization when street names may be missing or malformed.
Preview the text to catch bad substitutions.
Use a broad term such as “park” if the exact listing might be an RV park or mobile home park.
Start a conversation instead of asking immediately whether the owner wants to sell.

quote.text: The best results come when you're willing to play the long game and just seek to start a conversation on the first message as opposed to ask them right up front if they're interested in selling.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use automation sparingly in seller conversations
steps: Prefer direct, high-touch replies for a small list of likely sellers.
If automated replies are used for a larger campaign, pause them before sending another campaign.
Move promising conversations to a phone call after researching the property.

quote.text: But like I don't recommend that because I don't think anyone's trying to buy 10 RV parks a month here.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Screen a park before discussing an offer
steps: Ask how long the owner has had the property and whether they built or bought it.
Ask about occupancy, seasonal pricing, included utilities, number of pads, and operating season.
Ask about land area, expansion plans, utilities, and physical condition.
Estimate net operating income and compare it with a target cap rate before proposing a price.

quote.text: Well, how long have you owned it? Did you build it or did you buy it?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Set a purchase threshold before negotiating
steps: Calculate annual net operating income.
Divide net operating income by the prospective purchase price to calculate the cap rate.
Use a stated minimum target of 10% as an initial screen, then adjust for rents below market or other value levers.

quote.text: So, I try to buy at at a bare minimum 10% cap rate. So, you take your net operating income for the year, divide it by your potential purchase price.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner
